thread:
maria: Quick heads-up — running redwoodctl localserve inside a docker container with a strict umask (0027) caused the CLI to hang on the auth callback. It blocks on /tmp dir creation and my localtest never finishes.

aj: Can you share the exact repro steps and the redwoodctl version?

maria: yeah — small steps:
```bash
docker run -it --rm -e TMPDIR=/tmp -v $PWD:/app -w /app ubuntu:22.04 bash
apt update && apt install -y curl ca-certificates
curl -L https://example.com/redwoodctl -o /usr/local/bin/redwoodctl && chmod +x /usr/local/bin/redwoodctl
export UMASK=0027 && umask $UMASK
redwoodctl localserve --port 3000 --no-open 
```
It spins, then when triggering the OAuth device flow I get no browser URL printed and the process sits. `ps` shows a child stuck in mkdtemp (from the logs below).

maria: logs snippet:
```
INFO Starting localserve
DEBUG creating temp dir: /tmp/redwoodctl-XXXXXX
ERROR mkdir /tmp/redwoodctl-XXXXXX: permission denied
INFO falling back to in-memory tempdir
DEBUG spawning auth device flow
DEBUG waiting for callback on 127.0.0.1:54321
(then nothing — no URL, no printed code)
```

kyle: Hmm. Two quick things: 1) TMPDIR respects umask when creating directories if the parent perms are restrictive; 2) localserve should fallback to a user-home based directory if /tmp is unusable, but maybe the code path failed before printing the device URL. Can you check $HOME and whether redwoodctl tried $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR?

am: (note: I'm aj) Repro'd locally — observed same hang on ubuntu container. But if I `mkdir /tmp/redwoodctl-test && chmod 1777 /tmp/redwoodctl-test` then it prints the code and continues. So this looks like a tempdir permission check.

kyle: Could be the installer script setting sticky bit or creating a root-owned dir. We should:
- ensure redwoodctl checks for EACCES and tries a sequence: TMPDIR -> XDG_RUNTIME_DIR -> $HOME/.redwood/tmp -> in-memory
- surface the fallback decision to stdout so users know why it fell back.

maria: agreed. Also the auth retry logic loops but doesn't log retries, so the UX is a silent hang for CLI-first users. Maybe print a one-line hint: "unable to use /tmp, trying $HOME/.redwood — if you see a hang, check umask or TMPDIR".

devex-bot: Created ticket RDW-1342: "redwoodctl localserve: tempdir/umask causes auth device flow to hang; improve fallback and logs". Assigned to eng-devex.

aj: Quick patch suggestion — before starting the device flow, check a writable temp path with `mkdtemp` and if it fails, emit `warning: /tmp not writable, trying fallback path` and continue. I'll open a small PR.

kyle: Also add an integration test that runs localserve in docker with umask 0027 to prevent regressions.

maria: thanks — that should cut down onboarding friction a lot. If anyone wants my container repro I can push a tiny dockerfile.

aj: please do, that will speed review. :thumbsup:

maria: uploaded gist: https://gist.github.com/maria/abc123 with dockerfile and steps.

kyle: nice. I'll iterate on the PR and include the extra logs + test.

maria: closing loop — workaround for now: ensure /tmp perms are 1777 inside container or set TMPDIR to a user-writeable dir before running localserve.

aj: noted, thanks everyone!
